items.q: Unilateral lateral wall mass in 55 year old man recurring after removal, with focal hyperostosis on CT, most likely is what?
items.exp: Inverted papilloma attaches laterally with bony reaction, recurs if origin not drilled, and associates with squamous carcinoma in up to about a tenth, mandating complete excision and surveillance.
r: Incorrect. Polyps are usually bilateral allergic.
Correct. Inverted papilloma of lateral wall.
Incorrect. Antrochoanal is youthful maxillary polyp.
Incorrect. Turbinate swelling shrinks and is sensitive.
items.kp: One sided, recurs, bone spot: inverted papilloma.

items.q: Why is clinic biopsy forbidden in suspected juvenile angiofibroma?
o: Profuse haemorrhage from vascular tumour without control
items.exp: Angiofibromas are dense vascular masses in adolescents where imaging is diagnostic and biopsy can flood; angiography with embolisation then resection in theatre is pathway.
r: Incorrect. Not infection issue.
Correct. Biopsy can cause catastrophic bleeding.
Incorrect. Seeding is not concern; bleeding is.
Incorrect. It is benign histology.
items.kp: Vascular teen tumour: pictures, not biopsies.

items.q: Ethmoid adenocarcinoma occupational association is classically what?
items.exp: Hardwood dust (beech, oak) deposited in olfactory and ethmoid region causes intestinal type adenocarcinoma after long latency; nickel instead associates squamous carcinoma of sinuses.
r: Incorrect. Nickel links squamous type.
Correct. Hardwood dust, ethmoid adenocarcinoma.
Incorrect. Asbestos is pleural and peritoneal.
Incorrect. Coal is lung disease pattern.
items.kp: Carpenter ethmoid cancer from hardwood dust.

items.q: Inverted papilloma malignant association requiring surveillance is transformation or coexistence with what?
items.exp: Synchronous or later squamous carcinoma within papilloma occurs in roughly a tenth spectrum, so histology of entire specimen and long endoscopic follow up are mandatory.
r: Incorrect. Melanoma is separate mucosal tumour.
Correct. Squamous carcinoma association.
Incorrect. Lymphoma arises independently midline.
Incorrect. Sarcoma rare different tumour.
items.kp: Papilloma hides squamous cancer in one in ten.

items.q: Necrotic destructive midline nasal lesion with EBV positivity and systemic fever most suggests what?
o: Extranodal NK T cell lymphoma, nasal type
items.exp: EBV driven NK T lymphoma destroys midface (old lethal midline granuloma) with necrosis and systemic symptoms, needing deep edge biopsies, EBV viral load and chemo radiation haematology care.
r: Incorrect. GPA lacks EBV driver and responds differently.
Correct. NK T lymphoma nasal type.
Incorrect. Cocaine may coexist but EBV tumour dominates picture.
Incorrect. Destruction exceeds simple hole.

items.q: MRI in sinonasal tumour planning adds what over CT chiefly?
o: Separates tumour from retained secretions and maps orbit, dura and perineural spread
items.exp: Secretions trapped behind tumour mimic mass on CT; MRI signal separates them and defines orbital, intracranial and skull base invasion for staging and resection or radiation fields.
r: Incorrect. CT wins bone anatomy.
Correct. Soft tissue separation and invasion mapping.
Incorrect. Dental bone is CT strength.
Incorrect. MRI is decisive for extent.
items.kp: CT for bone, MRI for tumour truth.

items.q: Olfactory neuroblastoma arises from which site and often presents how?
o: Olfactory cleft high in nose; unilateral obstruction, epistaxis, anosmia
items.exp: Esthesioneuroblastoma grows from olfactory epithelium superiorly (Kadish staging by extension), often dumbbell into anterior cranial fossa, treated with surgery plus radiation pathways.
r: Incorrect. Maxillary tumours cause dental signs.
Correct. High olfactory origin with smell loss.
Incorrect. Nasopharyngeal cancer gives that pattern.
Incorrect. Skin tumours differ.
items.kp: Smell gone, high mass: olfactory tumour.

items.q: Saddle nose with septal perforation, crusting plus haematuria and lung nodules points to which systemic disease needing ANCA?
items.exp: Upper airway destruction with pulmonary renal small vessel vasculitis and PR3 ANCA defines GPA; nasal limited disease still scars septum and saddle before systemic declaration.
r: Incorrect. Sarcoid infiltrates but renal lung pattern differs.
Correct. GPA vasculitis triad pattern.
Incorrect. Polychondritis attacks cartilage including ears.
Incorrect. Lupus pernio is sarcoid skin of nose, not perforating vasculitis.

items.q: Frontal sinus osteoma is most commonly discovered how and managed how?
o: Incidental imaging finding; observe unless obstructing, growing or symptomatic
items.exp: Slow benign bone tumours are frequent incidental findings; surgery follows sinus obstruction, mucocele, orbital or intracranial growth, or headache attribution after evaluation.
r: Incorrect. Most are silent findings.
Correct. Incidental, observe selectively.
Incorrect. Not vascular bleeders.
Incorrect. Adult incidental pattern.
items.kp: Quiet bone lump on scan: watch it.

items.q: Cocaine induced midline lesion is separated from GPA most helpfully by what?
o: History and toxicology, often palatal necrosis, ANCA can be atypically positive in cocaine use
items.exp: Cocaine (and levamisole adulterant) destroys septum and palate mimicking vasculitis serologically; confidential history, drug testing with consent and absence of systemic vasculitis organs guide, and cessation is treatment.
r: Incorrect. Sizes overlap completely.
Correct. Exposure history and systemic absence.
Incorrect. Age overlaps.
Incorrect. Both crust heavily.
items.kp: Ask the powder question in midline destruction.
